summary.text: 月 is an indivisible pictograph of a half moon. Shang inscriptions use it both for the moon and for calendar months, the latter associated with the moon’s waxing and waning cycle.

formation.text: The whole graph depicts a half moon; its strokes are not separate semantic or phonetic components. Ancient forms are described as moon pictures, while later forms become less pictorial before the regular shape stabilizes.

components.text: The whole graph 月 is a pictorial depiction of a half moon. Treat it as one indivisible picture, not as a combination of smaller components.

history.text: The curated oracle-script image is a modern rendering linked to a specific Sinica record. The seal-script image is a modern reconstruction of the Shuowen tradition. They provide graphic comparisons, not proof of a precise sequence or first attestation.

A reported paleographic analysis says 月 and 夕 once shared a moon-shaped graph; an interior dot did not initially distinguish them. Later graphic specialization associated the dotted form with 月 and the undotted form with 夕. The date and mechanism of this differentiation remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The cited sources report Shang uses for both the moon and calendar months but do not establish which use came first or the character’s precise first dated attestation.
Proposed word-family and cognate explanations are not assessed here, and no particular proposal is endorsed.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone period; precise dating unresolved
senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 月 for the moon, including in an eclipse context. This is the earliest documented use represented here; the evidence does not fix its first dated occurrence.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone and bronze periods; precise dating unresolved
senses.text: 月 is also reported in Shang calendrical notation for named months. This use is associated with the moon’s waxing and waning cycle, but its chronology relative to the moon sense is unresolved.
Moonlight is recorded as a later dictionary sense; its first occurrence and development are not established here.
The character is documented with a monthly or each-month sense, but its first occurrence and chronology are not detailed here.
A dictionary records a use for round forms resembling the moon; when and how it developed are unresolved.
A time-counting classifier or unit use is recorded, but its first occurrence and relation to the calendar-month sense are not detailed here.
A surname use is recorded, with no evidence here for its first occurrence or origin.

developments.text: The calendar-month sense is explained through the moon’s recurring waxing and waning. Since both uses are reported in Shang material, this explanation does not establish a chronological transition.

limitations.text: Later dictionary senses are recorded, but their first occurrences and semantic transitions are not detailed here.
Supplied readings concern 月 as a whole; no component-to-character sound comparison applies because no phonetic component is proposed.

items.period: Shang oracle-bone script; source record is identified as 簠天1, 合33694, 歷組
items.caption: This oracle-script form has a long central stroke and a curved outer stroke that frame a crescent-shaped opening, a shape consistent with 月 as a moon pictograph.
items.alt: Black glyph with a long vertical stroke beside a curved outer stroke, leaving a crescent-shaped opening.
items.selection_reason: The visible strokes match the documented half-moon pictographic account. The form is identified with a specific Shang oracle-bone record.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on the Commons page for the Sinica-derived image.

items.period: Shuowen small-seal script tradition; the image is a modern vector reconstruction
items.caption: This small-seal form has a rounded enclosing outline, an interior cross-stroke, and a curved extension below.
items.alt: Black rounded glyph with an oval outline, a short interior stroke, a cross-stroke, and a long curved lower extension.
items.selection_reason: It offers a useful graphic comparison: the rounded, less crescent-like outline shows how a later script tradition rendered 月. It is a modern reconstruction of the Shuowen seal-script tradition.
items.rights: Public domain dedication for the SVG representation, as stated on the Commons file page.
